Spotify Just Gained 7% in a Week. What Will It Take to Hit $700? ©@twinsterphoto via Canva; @Adam Smigielski from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) stock is up 7% in the past week, mostly after a report that it plans a paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027, possibly at $4 to $5 a month extra.

The add-on would let Spotify charge for AI just as growth in Premium revenue per user slows after its price increases.

Analysts already expect normalized earnings per share to rise about 45% from 2025 to 2027, and the remix service isn't in those estimates.

JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley recently raised the target price to $700. This works out to about 44x expected earnings, below the stock's average since early 2024, so reaching it depends mainly on the Q4 report in early February.

Spotify is up 7% in the past week. Over the same stretch, the Nasdaq 100 fell 7%, and the S&P 500 slipped 5%. As of Thursday's close, the stock sits about 4% below its 52-week high.

$700 is about 14% above that close. Getting there would take two things: a new way to charge subscribers, and a strong holiday quarter.

What exactly happened

The biggest gain came on Friday, Oct. 30. Early that morning, the Financial Times reported that Spotify plans a paid AI service for remixes and covers:

Timing: Q1 of 2027, possibly around the Grammy Awards in February

Price: possibly $4 to $5 a month on top of a subscription

Labels: Universal Music Group, indie-label group Merlin and Believe have signed on, while Sony Music and Warner Music are still negotiating

On Monday, Citi raised its target to $715 from $620 and kept its Buy rating. Wednesday's gain came with no company news, as internet stocks rallied with the market.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Spotify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Spotify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Spotify's Analyst Ratings

A new way to charge more

Spotify could use one. Its Q3 beat its own guidance on Oct. 22, and price increases did much of the work: Premium revenue grew 17% to €4.49 billion while subscribers grew 9%.

That boost is fading. Premium revenue per user rose 7.5% at constant currency in Q3. For Q4, management guides 4.5% to 5% as Spotify laps price increases in more than 150 markets.

At $4 to $5, the remix add-on would cost roughly a third as much as the $12.99 US individual plan. It would also have Spotify making money from AI, which investors have mostly treated as a threat.

Last month, Jefferies analyst James Heaney called the platform "highly defensible against AI disintermediation fears." The add-on goes further: subscribers would pay extra for the AI itself.

title: Spotify Is Up 33% in Six Months: Take Profits, or Buy More?
detail:
Spotify Is Up 33% in Six Months: Take Profits, or Buy More?
Rexielyn Diaz
Sun, November 1, 2026 at 4:22 PM MST 5 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Spotify Is Up 33% in Six Months: Take Profits, or Buy More? ©twinsterphoto and Eugenio Marongiu via Canva
Key Takeaways

Spotify jumped 6.5% on Friday to $593 and is up 33% in six months, as Universal Music reported a subscription beat the same day.

Third-quarter operating income of €672 million beat guidance, and co-CEO Alex Norström said "this was a quarter where we did what we said."

Fourth-quarter guidance needs 10 million net subscriber adds and a 15.8% operating margin, both well above what the third quarter delivered.

The stock trades at 37.5x forward earnings with a $642 average target, so the February report has to confirm the margin step-up.

In July, Spotify stock was down about 16% for the year. Investors were punishing it for spending.

That mood is gone. Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) jumped 6.5% on Friday to close at $593, and it is now up 33% over six months. The stock sits about 11% below its 52-week high of $669.

Friday's move came as Universal Music Group (UMG), the world's biggest record label, reported subscription growth that beat expectations. That's a reversal for UMG, whose stock fell about 25% in July when its underlying subscription growth missed. On the same day, the Financial Times reported that Spotify is aiming for a 2027 launch of an AI remix service.

Those stories connect. Spotify and UMG signed licensing deals in May covering fan-made covers and remixes, the groundwork any remix product needs.

So at $593, do you take profits or buy more?

A quarter of small beats

Spotify's third quarter, reported October 22, edged past its own guidance almost everywhere.

Revenue rose 16% to €4.97 billion, or 14% in constant currency.

Gross margin hit a third-quarter record of 33.0%, up 136 basis points.

Premium subscribers reached 306 million on 6 million net adds, 1 million above guidance.

Operating income of €672 million topped the €670 million guide as marketing and personnel costs came in light. "This was a quarter where we did what we said," co-CEO Alex Norström said in the results release.

Net income fell 42% to €518 million, but that drop sits below the operating line. The year-ago quarter carried €197 million of gains on since-repaid exchangeable notes plus a tax benefit.

Gross margin is the trend that matters…

Spotify Technology (SPOT): gross margin (%), quarterly, Q3 2024–Q3 2026 (TIKR)

Management guided fourth-quarter gross margin to 33.8%, so the climb isn't finished.

Pricing is doing the lifting

Premium revenue grew 17% to €4.49 billion, well ahead of 9% subscriber growth. Price increases and add-ons like Audiobooks+ fill that gap.

That's faster growth than the labels Spotify pays. Its Premium revenue grew 15% in constant currency last quarter, more than double the 6.7% underlying subscription growth UMG posted in its second quarter.

title: Spotify Is Up 16% in a Month. Is Its Q3 Report Really That Good?
detail:
Spotify Is Up 16% in a Month. Is Its Q3 Report Really That Good?
Nikko Henson
Sun, November 1, 2026 at 2:01 PM MST 3 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Spotify Is Up 16% in a Month. Is Its Q3 Report Really That Good? ©@twinsterphoto via Canva; @Adam Smigielski from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Spotify Technology (SPOT) stock climbed 16% in the month through October 22, outperforming the Nasdaq-100, which declined 6% over the same period.

Spotify added 6 million premium subscribers, beating guidance by 1 million, while revenue increased 16% and operating income grew 15%.

Operating expenses increased 26%, making spending discipline essential to maintaining profitability improvements.

At approximately 36x forward earnings and 5% above Wall Street's average price target, Spotify looks slightly overvalued, making it a hold rather than a fresh buy.

What Happened?

Spotify Technology (SPOT:NYSE) stock surged 16% in the month through October 22, closing at approximately $584 as strong third-quarter results fueled investor optimism.

The rally significantly outperformed the Nasdaq-100, which declined 6% over the same period, with much of Spotify's advance coming after its October 22 earnings announcement.

According to Spotify's third-quarter earnings report, the company added 6 million premium subscribers, exceeding guidance by 1 million and bringing its total to 306 million. Revenue increased 16% to €4.97 billion, while operating income grew 15% to €672 million.

However, earnings per share of €2.48 missed analysts' €2.80 estimate, largely because of lower finance income and higher taxes rather than weaker operating performance.

Finance income declined to €62 million from €262 million, while a €72 million tax benefit a year earlier became a €187 million tax expense.

Spotify's gross margin improved every year since 2022, increasing from 25.0% to 32.0% in 2025.

Spotify Technology (SPOT): gross margin (%), fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

Third-quarter gross margin reached a record 33.0%, while management projected 33.8% for the fourth quarter, alongside €820 million in operating income.

Spending Remains Spotify's Biggest Challenge

Spotify's operating expenses increased 26% to €967 million, partly driven by marketing and AI computing investments, while free cash flow declined 9% to €735 million.

Co-CEO Alex Norström said Spotify's "costs are moderating, and there is more runway ahead."

Management's fourth-quarter guidance implies operating expense growth could slow to approximately 17.5%, with operating margins approaching 15.8%, compared with 13.5% in Q3.

That improvement could support stronger earnings growth if Spotify maintains subscriber momentum while controlling expenses.

Is Spotify Stock Undervalued or Overvalued?

Spotify delivered a strong third quarter, but its valuation already reflects considerable optimism about future profitability.

title: Spotify Stock Is Down 26%. Should You Buy the Dip, or Run for the Hills?
detail:
Spotify Stock Is Down 26%. Should You Buy the Dip, or Run for the Hills?
Anthony Di Pizio, The Motley Fool
October 30, 2026 6 min read
SPOT
NVDA
MU
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

When it comes to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, investors tend to think of chip giants like Nvidia or Micron Technology. But AI is starting to create value for many companies, even those not operating at the industry's frontier, and that spells an opportunity for investors.

Spotify (NYSE: SPOT) runs the world's largest music streaming platform, and it's betting big on AI to enhance the listening experience, which is boosting engagement and, therefore, revenue. The company reported a strong set of operating results for the third quarter of 2026 (ended Sept. 30) last week, which sent its stock soaring by more than 11%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But the stock is still down 26% from last year's record high as I write this on Oct. 27, so should investors take this opportunity to buy the dip, or will the recent recovery run out of steam?

Image source: Getty Images.
Artificial intelligence is transforming Spotify

Most music streaming services offer the same content catalog, because a small handful of record labels control most of the industry's rights, and they want their artists to reach as many listeners as possible. That means the primary way Spotify can differentiate its platform from the competition is by delivering a better user experience, and AI is central to its strategy.

AI is embedded in Spotify's recommendation algorithm, where it learns what type of music each user likes, so it can feed them more of it. AI also powers a growing number of features, like Prompted Playlist which will curate a basket of songs based on a description provided by the user. But management is aiming to turn Spotify into the world's first agentic media platform, which will introduce a range of unique capabilities, and some of them are already live.

For example, users can ask Spotify to analyze their listening history dating all the way back to 2008, and surface their favorite songs. It can also ask the platform to mix tracks together to create the perfect playlist, organized by factors like beats per minute. It can also recap an audiobook the user is listening to, up until the point they previously stopped.

Spotify can integrate with third-party agentic systems like OpenAI's Dots and Meta Platforms' Muse, enabling users to control their audio environment while completing other tasks. For example, users can ask Muse to build a playlist through Spotify, tailored to a specific road-trip destination.
